about: The later stages of each search, in order, to a recordable result, and what each costs: progress.py (stages_of) estimates each later stage from the run's own count of the unit each part is per, that part's CPU seconds per unit (cpu: median and the 5% and 95% quantiles of its uncertainty), its processes, and the share of a core the run's workers get now, taken for every process of every later stage (so 9 processes at once at a share q are taken to have 9 q of the machine's cores: an assumption).  A later stage has phases, one after another; a phase has lanes, at once, and lasts as long as its longest lane (ideal overlap, an approximation: the time a pipeline loses is not in it); a lane has parts, one after another; all of it replicate by replicate.  CPU over the share is a CPU-limited time, without storage waits.  What a part's conditions call unmeasured is not in the estimate.  A stage with run is a run of its own, surveyed by progress.py while it runs.  432:12's chain written by scratch/stages-cram-20261101/derive.py from its measurements (derive.json there); 288:10's as scratch/stages-20261031/derive.py wrote it (derive.json there), each of its parts the one part of the one lane of its stage's one phase.

phases.conditions: arm assemble: fanout.assemble's loop body for one done job (jid, Lex.status, load, the box, root, witness and brief checks, frontier, the cut's check, walked, jobs, passed, the todo push through pairs), its statements asserted verbatim against fanout.assemble's source.  The driver assembles alone, serially, after its last job and before it writes its finish (fanout.py run, assemble, passed its default). Sample: 300 job files drawn at random (seed 1) from the 107,976 of scratch/fanout432/jobs (4,318,134 tokens). CPU by time.process_time_ns of one process at nice 19, one BLAS thread, on the installed CRAM files (fanout.py f56e2346..., reprove.py 631b3fbe..., fanout_code cd6521ed...), the live machine loaded (load average 16.1 to 66.6; 432:12's 8 workers running since 04:44:52 PST, and ps at its end showing macOS's mobileassetd and modelcatalogd busy), 2026-11-01 04:47:22 PST to 2026-11-01 04:50:23 PST.  Each file was read before its timed arms, so its reads were warm, and process_time leaves storage waits out: with the share, a CPU-limited time, without cold reads or reads in parallel.  The harness made its dicts and lists anew for each file and collected garbage untimed, so the allocator and caches of a walk over the whole corpus are not reproduced.  Each arm's time includes releasing its own result (measure.py's timed, quals_measure.py). Rate: the arm's CPU over its tokens, summed over the files.  Band: 5% and 95% of 2,000 bootstrap replicates of that rate, each a resample of whole file records; sampling uncertainty over the measured corpus only, not the future jobs' mix, the machine's scheduling or the model's error. Beside it: the assembly candidate's per-job checks, without the pairs push, 835 ns a token (scratch/claude-astra-20261031/assembly/logs/bench_walk.json). Unmeasured, and not in the estimate: unmoved (focus.replay of the run's chunks), symmetric's invariant of each case, the checks over the journal's records (the sessions' codes, the probes, every job_end at the end) and set(walked) == set(done).

phases.conditions: The candidate scratch/boxsplit288-b-20261030/candidate/boxsplit.py (sha256 739b54eb..., EXTENSION ((11, 13), (1000, 2000000))) on the certbb of 2026-10-30 19:42 (fastlp), nice 19, one BLAS thread, load 110-166: 40 uniform leaves (u60f), 3 heavy (heavy4f) and 8 loose (loose8), loose leaves censored at 150-300 s; per leaf, base + own children by slack band, weighted by round a's 1,000-leaf survey.  Band: that estimate's bootstrap. The installed scratch/x288/boxsplit.py (sha256 6cd66f4a...) is not this code: on the uniform leaves it took 2.03 times this CPU (1.81-2.21), on loose leaves less; until the candidate is installed this cost is a floor.  The step runs v5.PROCESSES = 10 workers.

scratch/x288/handoff288.handoff on prefixes of the live journal, one process at nice 19: 3.21 CPU s for 30,102 closed leaves, 15.04 for 120,533.  Median the larger's per leaf, low end the smaller's, high end the growth between them applied once more: the handoff will close about ten times as many leaves.

The final pass splits again every node above the bottom that the journal holds UNKNOWN, as each restart of the pass did: the worker seconds of those splits over the open leaves walked past, at the restarts of 2026-10-30 00:04, 17:23 and 19:43 (0.06003, 0.06757, 0.07090 s an open leaf: low, median and high), times the share of a core the current pass's 10 workers got, 0.4258 (ps: their CPU over their seconds of running, the pauses left out).  The three restarts ran at shares not measured, so the band mixes the cost's spread with the machine's.  Leaves out the journal's loading and the startup control, minutes.
